sources.citation: Vogler, Pierre 2017. Contribution a la classification des langues kru (Niger-Congo). Manuscript, HAL hal-01574391v2, 74 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent anywhere (grep accent/stress: only 'mettre l'accent sur' idiom). Sec. 2.4: tone systems of three (bassa, klao, neyo) or four registers (grebo, bete, vata). Its 'grebo' data are Innes/Payne (Glebo).

sources.citation: Hartell, Rhonda L. (ed.) 1993. Alphabets of Africa. Dakar: UNESCO Regional Office (BREDA). Sheet 'Liberia: Grebo (Chlehpo dialect) (Kru)' [LIBTRALO orthography, 'still in the testing stages'] (= PHOIBLE inventory AA 725, mapped by PHOIBLE to nort2810).
sources.note: Nothing. One-page phoneme/grapheme list with four tones (top, high, mid, low; high and mid unmarked 'in grammatical and/or contextual complementary distribution'); no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, language nort2810 / inventory 725 'grebo (AA 725)' (Chanard & Hartell, from Hartell 1993 / Chanard 2006).
sources.note: Segment and tone inventory only (36 segments incl. 4 tone letters); no stress information.

sources.citation: Innes, Gordon 1966. An Introduction to Grebo. London: School of Oriental and African Studies. Ch.2 'Sounds' pp.14-15, ch.1 'Orthography' pp.11-13, contents, ch.6-7 excerpt (Rosetta Project excerpts on archive.org: rosettaproject_gbo_phon-1, _orth-1, _contents-1, _morsyn-1).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Old Widener 2235.28.28 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: The excerpted pages (consonants, vowels, root shapes, four tone levels) contain no stress statement; Innes's stress passage is on pp.18-19 (not in the excerpt; carried by StressTyp2 and already catalogued under sout2826). Innes's 'Grebo' is Glebo/Gedebo of Cape Palmas = Southern Grebo (sout2826), not Northern Grebo.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Grebo language' (wikitext fetched sources via API).
sources.note: Innes-based consonant/vowel tables and a note on tone; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record nort2810 and reference records (Berry & Innes 1957 'Notes on the phonetics of the Grebo language of Liberia' pp.287-298; Innes 1960 'An outline of the Grebo verbal system'; Innes 1962 'Morphological units in Grebo'; Payne 1864/1882 Grebo grammar; LIBTRALO 1997 primer; TILL 1976/1978 primers; Ingemann & Duitsman 1976/77; Necollin & Meyers 1998 dictionary).
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Bibliographic records only. All the analytic 'Grebo' works (Wilson, Payne, Berry & Innes, Innes) are on Cape Palmas Glebo = Southern Grebo; they are attached to gbo by automatic translation of Maho's code. No grammar, sketch or phonology of a Northern Grebo dialect is listed (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0; MED = Innes 1966 dictionary).
